newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh's Ershad invites party rebels to talks.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh's Ershad invites party rebels to talks.

text.p: Former Bangladesh president Hossain Mohammad Ershad has invited rebels in his Jatiya Party to talks in a bid to avert a split triggered by his love life, sources said on Wednesday.
They said the meeting was expected any time following the Moslem Eid al-Adha festival on Friday.

Ershad's party leadership came under threat when the rebels in Jatiya, the country's third-biggest political group, on Thursday asked him to quit his post as party chairman after he publicly confessed to an extramarital love affair.

In a newspaper interview, Ershad said that he had proposed to Zinat Hossain, wife of former industry secretary Mosharraf Hossain. A few weeks earlier, Ershad celebrated his birthday with Zinat, instead of his wife Begum Roushan.

"(The rebels) are doing crucial arithmetic of loss and gain," one party source told Reuters. "Jatiya without Ershad will lose much weight, while without three giants it will be equally affected," he said.

The three, former prime ministers Mizanur Rahman Chowdhury and Kazi Zafar Ahmed and former deputy prime minister Shah Moazzem Hossain, recently asked Ershad to transfer the party's leadership to them.
"The three rebel leaders have already been invited for the dialogue," Ershad's aide and senior party leader Naziur Rahman told the Daily Star on Tuesday.

The rebel leaders in a joint statement last week said Ershad had "turned the party into his own property and indulged in activities that not only tarnished his personal image but disturbed the party's rank and file".

The 68-year-old army general turned president, ousted in a popular uprising in 1990 and later jailed until this January, moved to save his career on Friday and dropped Zinat, his lover for 14 years and a fellow Jatiya Party legislator, from the party presidium.
The move did little to satisfy his foes.
"It's too little, too late," said rebel Kazi Zafar Ahmed on Saturday. "I don't see any reason for us to stop short of his resignation."
But fellow party rebel Mizanur Rahman Chowdhury appeared to soften his stance. He told Banglabazar Patrika newspaper on Wednesday that the party wanted Ershad "to correct himself".
"Differences of opinion are nothing new in politics...and these can be overcome," he said.
The Jatiya Party's newspaper, Dainik Janata, said on Wednesday that most of the 33 Jatiya legislators had reassured Ershad of their support.
